course.title: EcoSort: Sort It Right!
course.intro: Learn which bin your waste belongs in, play a quick sorting game, then test yourself with a 5-question quiz.

bins.label: Recycle
bins.description: Clean paper, plastic bottles, glass and metal cans.

bins.label: Compost
bins.description: Fruit scraps and garden waste that break down naturally.

bins.label: Landfill
bins.description: Things that can’t be recycled or composted, like chip packets.

items.label: Newspaper
items.hint: Clean paper can be made into new things.

items.label: Soda can
items.hint: Empty metal cans can be recycled.

items.label: Chip packet
items.hint: Chip packets are mixed materials that can’t be recycled in most systems.

items.label: Plastic bottle
items.hint: Empty plastic bottles are recyclable in many local programs.

items.label: Apple core
items.hint: Fruit scraps can become nutrient-rich compost.

items.label: Broken pen
items.hint: Broken pens are made of mixed materials.

items.label: Tea leaves
items.hint: Tea leaves are natural waste and can compost.

quiz.question: Which bin should a banana peel go in?

feedback.correct: Well done! Fruit peels break down naturally.
feedback.incorrect: Fruit peels break down naturally, so compost is the best choice.

quiz.question: Which bin should a used pizza box with grease go in?

feedback.correct: Correct! Food-soiled paper can be composted in many systems.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Grease spoils paper recycling, so compost it instead.

quiz.question: What should you do before recycling a soda can?

feedback.correct: Right! Empty containers are easier to process.
feedback.incorrect: Empty the can first, and check your local recycling rules.

quiz.question: Which item can usually go in the recycle bin?

feedback.correct: Correct! Clean paper can be recycled.
feedback.incorrect: Clean newspaper is recyclable in many local programs.

quiz.question: Where does a chip packet belong?

feedback.correct: Well done. Correct! Chip packets are mixed materials that can’t be recycled.
feedback.incorrect: Chip packets are mixed materials, so they usually belong in landfill.
